newsitem.title: USA: Boston Edison nuke seen at 100 pct Weds.
newsitem.headline: Boston Edison nuke seen at 100 pct Weds.

text.p: Boston Edison Co's 670 megawatt Pilgrim nuclear power plant was expected to reach 100 percent of capacity Wednesday after an unexpected shutdown for repairs which began Sept 17, a company spokesman said Wednesday.
"We are at about 86 percent of power right now, and we expect to reach 100 percent late today," said company spokesman Dave Tarantino.

The unit was shut after a leak was detected at a set of heat exchangers in a reactor building. During the outage, the company also completed some repairs in addition to correcting the heat exchanger problem, Tarantino said.
"We were able to do a couple of things that we had planned for the maintenance outage in February so hopefully things will go a little quicker then," he said.
The Pilgrim plant is scheduled to began a 35-day maintenance and refueling outage on February 1, 1997.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
